findings.description: The GUI HTML was extracted to a data file (templates/index.html) loaded at runtime via TEMPLATE_PATH = Path(__file__).parent/'templates'/'index.html' and TEMPLATE_PATH.read_text(). But pyproject.toml uses the setuptools backend with only [tool.setuptools.packages.find] and was deliberately left unchanged, and there is no [tool.setuptools.package-data]/MANIFEST.in. setuptools does NOT ship non-.py files by default, so a built wheel/sdist (pip install) will not contain index.html and the '/' route will raise FileNotFoundError on every request. The same applies to PyInstaller/frozen builds (health() reads sys.frozen), which won't bundle the data file. Tests and editable/launcher.sh installs run from the source tree, so '62 passed' completely masks this regression. This breaks the primary distribution path.

_render_page() calls TEMPLATE_PATH.read_text(encoding='utf-8') and render_template_string() on EVERY request to '/'. This re-reads the file from disk and recompiles the Jinja template per request (render_template_string bypasses Flask's template cache). The previous inline-PAGE approach compiled once. Read the template once at import/create_app time, or use render_template with the Jinja loader so it is cached.

_manager() silently falls back to the process-global get_manager() singleton when current_app.config['manager'] is absent/wrong type, whereas gui.py:_manager() raises RuntimeError for the identical condition. This divergence is dangerous: a misconfigured app (e.g. a test harness, or any create_app path that didn't set 'manager') will silently operate the global singleton, which may be bound to the real user's ~/Zomboid and ~/.pz-save-manager roots while the app intends overridden test roots. Backups/restores could hit the wrong filesystem location with no error. Make both modules behave identically (fail closed).

ConfigStore caches the file contents on first _load() and never invalidates the cache: there is no mtime check and no reload. Combined with the new design that creates multiple independent ConfigStore instances (cli.main() creates one, module-level default_store is another, create_app/run_gui may create/use others), writes through one instance are invisible to the others for the process lifetime, and external edits to config.json are never picked up. The 'backward-compatible' module-level get()/set_()/get_all() operate on default_store, which can diverge from the instance the GUI/CLI actually injected.

create_app() advertises dependency injection, but the module still instantiates a global app = create_app() at import time (constructing a WatcherManager and reading config as an import side effect), and run_gui() then MUTATES that global app's config and replaces app.config['manager'] with a brand-new WatcherManager instead of building a fresh app via create_app(...). This defeats the DI refactor: the manager passed/created by the CLI (ctx.obj['manager'] via get_manager) is discarded, run_gui ignores any 'manager' parameter (it has none), and global app state leaks across calls/imports. Importing gui for any reason spins up an unused WatcherManager.

On rename, the live save is re-registered with manager.watch(new_save) using NO arguments, so it silently reverts to the SaveWatcher defaults (debounce_seconds=5.0, backup_cooldown_seconds=300.0) and the manager's own roots, ignoring the user-configured debounce_seconds / backup_cooldown_minutes that every other watch() call site (api_watcher_toggle, api_watcher_save) passes explicitly. After a rename the watcher's behaviour silently changes.

CSRF token comparison uses a plain != ('request.headers.get(...) != CSRF_TOKEN'), which short-circuits and is not constant-time. Use secrets.compare_digest() to avoid leaking token bytes via timing. Minor for a localhost tool, but trivial to fix and this is the security boundary for all state-changing endpoints.

_coerce() does no range validation: port/backup_cooldown_minutes/max_auto_backups accept any int including negative or absurd values (e.g. port=999999, max_auto_backups=-1). api_config only catches ValueError/TypeError from int(), so out-of-range-but-parseable values are persisted and can break later startup or retention logic.

'auto_start_watcher' is accepted and persisted by api_config (and present in DEFAULTS), but no code path (run_gui/create_app/index) ever reads it to start the watcher. It is dead configuration that misleads the user into thinking enabling it will auto-start watching.

/health is unauthenticated and a plain GET (CSRF only guards POSTs), and discloses sys.executable, full python version, OS platform string, resolved absolute saves/backups paths (leaking the OS username), and a directory listing of the saves root. When the GUI is bound to a non-loopback host (gui --host 0.0.0.0 is permitted with no auth), this is information disclosure to the LAN. None of the endpoints have authentication beyond CSRF.

api_shutdown schedules os._exit(0) on a Timer. os._exit() terminates immediately without running finally blocks/atexit, so an in-flight auto-backup or restore in another thread can be killed mid-copy, potentially leaving an orphaned temp directory. manager.stop() is called but does not join in-progress create_backup work in the SaveWatcher timer thread.

summary: The refactor is structurally clean and all 62 tests pass, but the suite gives false confidence: it runs from the source tree and cannot catch the most serious regression. Extracting the template to templates/index.html without adding setuptools package-data/MANIFEST.in (pyproject.toml was deliberately left untouched) means built wheels and frozen builds will ship without the template and the '/' page will 500 with FileNotFoundError in production. Secondary concerns: the template is re-read and recompiled on every request; the DI is half-applied (module-level global app, run_gui mutates it, CLI's injected manager is discarded); routes_api silently falls back to the global singleton manager where gui.py fails closed, risking operations against the wrong filesystem roots; and ConfigStore's never-invalidated per-instance cache causes config divergence across the multiple stores the new design creates. Fix the packaging bug and add a test that exercises the installed/packaged template path before approving.
